Whole order (single paragraph, offsets 4545-6049 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8536.txt; 5 FR 3606, issue of Tuesday, September 10, 1940): signed September 6, 1940. It amends Executive Order No. 7747 of November 20, 1937 (a defensive sea area off San Clemente Island, California) by substituting one nautical mile for three hundred yards in its first paragraph and adding the area's name, and then reproduces EO 7747 as thus amended: the water surrounding the island out to one nautical mile beyond low-water mark is a defensive sea area, subject to the Commerce Department uses reserved by EO 6897; no vessel or craft may be navigated in it except as the Secretary of the Navy authorizes; and violators are subject to the penalties provided by law. The amendment instruction was performed on signing, but the reproduced text (area, vessel restriction, penalty) is the order's continuing content and has no term of its own. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 9787, signed October 5, 1946 (11 FR 11556), amends EO 7747 as amended by EO 8536 "to read as follows" and restates the whole text. Before: area out to one nautical mile beyond low-water mark. After: three hundred yards beyond low-water mark, except one hundred yards in Wilson Cove, and including the part of Pyramid Cove north of a described line; the vessel restriction and penalty paragraphs are carried over in the same terms. This rewrite replaces the whole section and changes the substance of the area. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (strike and insert) the clause continues, amended, and the amendment is recorded as a later event. A reviewer who reads EO 9787 as superseding this order's text would date the end at 1946-10-05 instead. First end: Executive Order 9894, signed September 23, 1947 (12 FR 6353, issue of September 25, 1947; filed September 23, 1947), which orders under section 44 of the Criminal Code (18 U.S.C. 96) that the San Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by EO 7747 as amended by EO 8536 and EO 9787, be discontinued. It names this order by number and discontinues the area that its text establishes. It has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing, 1947-09-23; the filing and printing dates are not effective dates.
